incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: P0 - AcmeCorp PrivateConnect path loss (packet loss > 30%), triggered 1765443208. Incident INC-2026-ACME-47 created. Paging Maya (oncall).
Maya (oncall): I’m paged, joining. Any short summary? :eyes:
Devon (support): Customer AcmeCorp reporting app errors and 5xx spikes, started ~09:12 UTC. They saw increased latency and TCP retransmits. I have their flow logs attached in ticket.
Maya (oncall): Thanks. Raj, can you grab BGP/state for the PrivateConnect attachments in eu-central-e az-e (region euc4 az-e)? Suspect route churn.
Raj (neteng): Looking. I see rapid BGP withdraws/advertises for the customer's prefixes on our east fabric. FIB churn counters jumping. Example from edge:
```
show ip bgp 203.0.113.0/24
Status: flapping, last change 09:11:34
Paths: 2 (AS-paths differ), next-hops 10.10.10.2, 10.10.11.2
Withdraws: 14 in 2m
```
Raj (neteng): Also seeing asymmetric path for some flows: traffic enters via privconn-az-e but returns via peer-az-c. Packet drops at our az-e TORs due to stale next-hop for a subset of prefixes.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact: confirmed AcmeOrg tenants in eu-west2 and eu-central experiencing errors. Important to mitigate fast — any quick mitigation? :ambulance:
Lucy (sre): Toggle idea: temporarily prefer the alternate PrivateConnect attachment (az-c) via route-preference policy to drain bad fabric. Can we push a route-map to prefer next-hop 10.10.11.2 for AcmeCorp prefixes? Risk: brief rehash but reduces drops.
Raj (neteng): I can apply a local route-map on the euc4 edge. Preparing command:
```
route-map ACME-FALLBACK permit 10
  match ip address prefix-list ACME-PFX
  set ip next-hop 10.10.11.2
```
Raj (neteng): Applying now to R-edge-euc4-02 (outbound to fabric). Pushing in 3...2...1.
incident-bot: Configuration push succeeded on R-edge-euc4-02 (job 7621). No config drift detected.
Maya (oncall): Devon, can you confirm with Acme if errors drop? Also watch for any amplification in other azs.
Devon (support): Messaging acme-ops now. @acme-ops can you confirm whether your requests are succeeding? They replied: "seeing a big drop in 5xx after ~09:15, still occasional request timeouts."
acme-ops: Confirmed, errors decreased from 26% to ~3% for our euc4 users. We'll keep testing.
Raj (neteng): FIB churn rate dropped substantially after route-map. Edge counters:
```
FIB-churn-rate: 1/min (was 150/min)
TCP retransmits: down 85%
```
Lucy (sre): Good. Next: schedule rollback plan and ask provider NOC for root cause. @NOC (provider) please confirm whether any recent fabric maintenance or route-reflect changes in az-e.
NOC (provider): We saw a transient route-reflector overload in az-e due to a malformed update from a peering device at 09:10 UTC. We throttled reflection but that caused some withdrawal storms. Root cause under investigation. We'll share postmortem.
Maya (oncall): Action list: 1) Keep route-map in place as temporary mitigation (Raj). 2) Coordinate with provider NOC for a permanent fix (Maya). 3) Keep customer updated (Devon). 4) Create follow-up runbook for FIB churn incidents (Lucy). Assigning owners in thread.
Raj (neteng): I'll leave the route-map in place and start a controlled rollback window at 11:00 UTC if no relapse. Will monitor RPKI/BGP anomalies too.
Devon (support): Sent update to customer, they acknowledged. Logged timeline into INC-2026-ACME-47.
Maya (oncall): Closing P0 page once stable metrics hold for 30m. Will run through post-incident checklist and link to ticket. Thanks all. :pray:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-ACME-47 severity downgraded to P1 at 1765443300 (mitigation in place).
